#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""SessionStart compact-hint reader (W173 P1(a) recompose).

Fires ONLY on SessionStart matcher=="compact" (post-auto-compact rehydrate boundary
per Anthropic CC hooks contract). Emits 4 sections to stdout via
hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext per https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks
SessionStart contract:

  (a) compact_hint.json (fresh <=300s) - pre-compact handoff content
  (b) MEMORY.md head 3K chars - Karpathy section 5 Layer-2 index
  (c) last-3 close-syntheses by mtime - Karpathy section 5 Layer-3 compiled wiki
  (d) git log -5 --oneline - recent commit chronology (Layer-1 chronological proxy)

Bounded <=9500 chars total (Anthropic CC 10K stdout cap safety margin).

Distinct from existing SessionStart matcher=="*" entries (session-lifecycle-hook,
context-mode-cache-heal, cli_path_audit) - this one ONLY fires on matcher=="compact"
to avoid noise on startup/resume events.

Sister-rule integration:
- sessionstart-preload-discipline.md section The contract (3-layer preload sequence)
- auto-compact-discipline.md Rank #5 (Karpathy section 5 3-layer progressive disclosure)
- karpathy-adapted.md section 5 Wiki Compounding Surface (Layer 1/2/3 mapping)
- fm20-path-drift-cascade.md (stale-belief-propagation defense at session-resume)
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import datetime as _dt
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

REPO_ROOT = Path("Z:/claude-sota-installed")
STATE_DIR = REPO_ROOT / ".claude" / "state"
HINT_PATH = STATE_DIR / "compact_hint.json"
MEMORY_INDEX = REPO_ROOT / ".claude" / "projects" / "Z--claude-sota-installed" / "memory" / "MEMORY.md"
TMP_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "tmp"
TELEMETRY_PATH = STATE_DIR / "sessionstart_compact_hint_reader.jsonl"

HINT_FRESH_SEC = 300       # <=300s sidecar freshness window
MEMORY_HEAD_CHARS = 3000   # Karpathy section 5 Layer-2 head portion
STDOUT_CAP_CHARS = 9500    # Anthropic 10K cap safety margin
GIT_LOG_LINES = 5          # recent-commit chronology


def _now_iso() -> str:
    # W187 round-2 codex T1 prescription #5: datetime.utcnow() deprecated in Python 3.12+
    # emits DeprecationWarning to stderr; SessionStart stderr is user-visible — pollutes rehydrate.
    # Replaced with timezone-aware datetime.now(timezone.utc); .isoformat() yields '+00:00' suffix,
    # .replace('+00:00', 'Z') preserves prior 'Z' suffix convention for ISO 8601 UTC.
    return _dt.datetime.now(_dt.timezone.utc).isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z")


def _read_stdin_payload() -> dict[str, Any]:
    try:
        raw = sys.stdin.read() or ""
        return json.loads(raw) if raw.strip() else {}
    except Exception:
        return {}


def _section_a_hint() -> str:
    """Section A: compact_hint.json fresh <=300s."""
    if not HINT_PATH.exists():
        return "## (a) compact_hint.json - ABSENT (no pre-compact handoff written)"
    try:
        age_sec = _dt.datetime.now().timestamp() - HINT_PATH.stat().st_mtime
        if age_sec > HINT_FRESH_SEC:
            return f"## (a) compact_hint.json - STALE ({age_sec:.0f}s > {HINT_FRESH_SEC}s cap)"
        with HINT_PATH.open(encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            data = json.load(fh)
        if not isinstance(data, dict) or data.get("version") != 1:
            return "## (a) compact_hint.json - INVALID schema"
        lines = [
            "## (a) compact_hint.json (fresh, version=1)",
            f"  ts: {data.get('ts')}",
            f"  current_goal: {data.get('current_goal')}",
            f"  test_state: {data.get('test_state')}",
            f"  next_action: {data.get('next_action')}",
            "  files_touched:",
        ]
        for f in (data.get("files_touched") or [])[:20]:
            lines.append(f"    - {f}")
        lines.append("  design_cites:")
        for c in (data.get("design_cites") or [])[:10]:
            lines.append(f"    - {c}")
        return "\n".join(lines)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
        return f"## (a) compact_hint.json - READ-ERROR: {exc!r}"


def _compact_hint_ready() -> bool:
    if not HINT_PATH.exists():
        return False
    try:
        if HINT_PATH.stat().st_size == 0:
            return False
        with HINT_PATH.open(encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            data = json.load(fh)
        return isinstance(data, dict) and data.get("version") == 1
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return False


def _section_b_memory_head() -> str:
    """Section B: MEMORY.md head 3K chars (Karpathy section 5 Layer-2 index)."""
    if not MEMORY_INDEX.exists():
        return "## (b) MEMORY.md - ABSENT"
    try:
        text = MEMORY_INDEX.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        head = text[:MEMORY_HEAD_CHARS]
        return f"## (b) MEMORY.md head ({len(head)} chars):\n{head}"
    except Exception as exc:
        return f"## (b) MEMORY.md - READ-ERROR: {exc!r}"


def _section_c_close_synthesis() -> str:
    """Section C: last-3 close-syntheses by mtime (Karpathy section 5 Layer-3)."""
    patterns = [
        list(TMP_DIR.glob("wave*close-synthesis*.md")),
        list(TMP_DIR.glob("wave*-fire*-close-synthesis-*.md")),
    ]
    files: list[Path] = []
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for grp in patterns:
        for p in grp:
            if p.name not in seen:
                files.append(p)
                seen.add(p.name)
    files.sort(key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime if p.exists() else 0, reverse=True)
    last3 = files[:3]
    if not last3:
        return "## (c) close-syntheses - NONE FOUND (empty Layer-3)"
    lines = [f"## (c) last-3 close-syntheses (total {len(files)}):"]
    for p in last3:
        try:
            mtime = _dt.datetime.fromtimestamp(p.stat().st_mtime, _dt.timezone.utc).isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z")
            size = p.stat().st_size
            # Read first 400 chars summary
            preview = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")[:400]
            lines.append(f"  - {p.name} ({size} B, mtime={mtime})")
            lines.append(f"    preview: {preview[:300]}...")
        except Exception as exc:
            lines.append(f"  - {p.name} READ-ERROR: {exc!r}")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _section_d_git_log() -> str:
    """Section D: git log -5 --oneline (Layer-1 chronological proxy)."""
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", str(REPO_ROOT), "log", f"-{GIT_LOG_LINES}", "--oneline"],
            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=3,
        )
        if result.returncode == 0:
            return f"## (d) git log -{GIT_LOG_LINES} --oneline:\n{result.stdout.strip()}"
        return f"## (d) git log - FAILED (rc={result.returncode}): {result.stderr.strip()[:200]}"
    except (FileNotFoundError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as exc:
        return f"## (d) git log - ERROR: {exc!r}"


def _append_telemetry(record: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    try:
        STATE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with TELEMETRY_PATH.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(json.dumps(record) + "\n")
    except Exception as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(f"[sessionstart_compact_hint_reader] telemetry failed: {exc!r}\n")


def main() -> int:
    payload = _read_stdin_payload()
    source = payload.get("source", "unknown")

    # Fire ONLY on matcher=="compact" - verified via payload.source per Anthropic CC contract
    # SessionStart payload.source in {startup, resume, clear, compact}
    if source != "compact":
        # No-op for non-compact SessionStart events
        _append_telemetry({
            "schema": "sessionstart_compact_hint_reader.v1",
            "ts": _now_iso(),
            "wire_event": "SessionStart",
            "source": source,
            "fired": False,
            "reason": "source!=compact",
        })
        return 0

    hint_present = _compact_hint_ready()

    # Build compact handoff context. Supplemental recall is useful only when a
    # PreCompact hint exists; without it, these sections become unconditional
    # reinflation on every post-compact SessionStart.
    body_parts = [
        "POST-AUTO-COMPACT REHYDRATE (W173 P1(a) compact-matcher reader)",
        "",
        _section_a_hint(),
    ]
    if not hint_present:
        body = "\n".join(body_parts)
        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
            "hookSpecificOutput": {
                "hookEventName": "SessionStart",
                "additionalContext": body,
            }
        }))

        _append_telemetry({
            "schema": "sessionstart_compact_hint_reader.v1",
            "ts": _now_iso(),
            "wire_event": "SessionStart",
            "source": source,
            "fired": True,
            "compact_hint_present": False,
            "stdout_chars": len(body),
        })
        return 0

    body_parts.extend([
        "",
        _section_b_memory_head(),
        "",
        _section_c_close_synthesis(),
        "",
        _section_d_git_log(),
    ])
    body = "\n".join(body_parts)

    # Cap to <=9500 chars
    if len(body) > STDOUT_CAP_CHARS:
        body = body[:STDOUT_CAP_CHARS - 30] + "\n... [TRUNCATED at 9500 chars]"

    # Emit via hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext per Anthropic CC contract
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
        "hookSpecificOutput": {
            "hookEventName": "SessionStart",
            "additionalContext": body,
        }
    }))

    _append_telemetry({
        "schema": "sessionstart_compact_hint_reader.v1",
        "ts": _now_iso(),
        "wire_event": "SessionStart",
        "source": source,
        "fired": True,
        "session_id": payload.get("session_id"),
        "agent_id": payload.get("agent_id"),
        "agent_type": payload.get("agent_type"),
        "model": payload.get("model"),
        "transcript_path": payload.get("transcript_path"),
        "compact_hint_present": hint_present,
        "supplemental_sections_emitted": hint_present,
        "body_chars": len(body),
    })

    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""PreCompact hint emitter (W173 P1(a) recompose).

  https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks (PreCompact contract)

CAVEAT (per W164 F38a Wave 82e codex T1): PreCompact stdout NOT directly model-visible
per Anthropic CC docs L661-663 verbatim (only UserPromptSubmit/UserPromptExpansion/
SessionStart route stdout to model context). PreCompact emits "Additional Instructions:"
via the compact-summary text seam; semantic effect verified per W164 F38a live probe.
SessionStart matcher=compact reader (File 4) is the primary post-compact rehydrate
path; this emitter is the pre-compact handoff.

Schema: .claude/schemas/compact_hint.v1.json (compact_hint.v1).
Sidecar: .claude/state/compact_hint.json (fresh <=300s; else fallback to MEMORY.md tail).

Per Anthropic CC 10K stdout cap (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks PreCompact
section): payload bounded <=9500 chars (safety margin).

Sister-rule integration:
- auto-compact-discipline.md Rank #3 (Pre-emptive /compact <hint>)
- sessionstart-preload-discipline.md section The contract (cross-session continuity)

- launch-discipline.md section Observable (telemetry to .claude/state/ JSONL)
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import datetime as _dt
import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

REPO_ROOT = Path("Z:/claude-sota-installed")
STATE_DIR = REPO_ROOT / ".claude" / "state"
HINT_PATH = STATE_DIR / "compact_hint.json"
MEMORY_INDEX = REPO_ROOT / ".claude" / "projects" / "Z--claude-sota-installed" / "memory" / "MEMORY.md"
TELEMETRY_PATH = STATE_DIR / "precompact_hint_emitter.jsonl"

HINT_FRESH_SEC = 300  # <=300s sidecar staleness window (5 min)
STDOUT_CAP_CHARS = 9500  # Anthropic CC 10K cap safety margin
MEMORY_TAIL_CHARS = 3000  # Karpathy section 5 Layer-2 fallback portion size


def _now_iso() -> str:
    return _dt.datetime.utcnow().isoformat() + "Z"


def _read_stdin_payload() -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Parse PreCompact hook stdin per https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks contract."""
    try:
        raw = sys.stdin.read() or ""
        return json.loads(raw) if raw.strip() else {}
    except Exception:
        return {}


def _load_fresh_hint() -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """Load compact_hint.json if exists AND mtime within HINT_FRESH_SEC."""
    if not HINT_PATH.exists():
        return None
    try:
        age_sec = _dt.datetime.now().timestamp() - HINT_PATH.stat().st_mtime
        if age_sec > HINT_FRESH_SEC:
            return None
        with HINT_PATH.open(encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            data = json.load(fh)
        if not isinstance(data, dict) or data.get("version") != 1:
            return None
        return data
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError):
        return None


def _load_memory_fallback() -> str:
    """Karpathy section 5 Layer-2 fallback when hint sidecar absent/stale."""
    if not MEMORY_INDEX.exists():
        return "(MEMORY.md not found - no Layer-2 fallback available)"
    try:
        text = MEMORY_INDEX.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        return text[-MEMORY_TAIL_CHARS:] if len(text) > MEMORY_TAIL_CHARS else text
    except Exception as exc:
        return f"(MEMORY.md read error: {exc!r})"


def _format_hint_payload(hint: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """Format compact_hint v1 fields into Additional-Instructions-style block."""
    lines = [
        "PRE-COMPACT HINT (compact_hint.v1)",
        f"  ts: {hint.get('ts', '?')}",
        f"  current_goal: {hint.get('current_goal', '?')}",
        f"  test_state: {hint.get('test_state', 'UNKNOWN')}",
        f"  next_action: {hint.get('next_action', '?')}",
        "",
        "files_touched:",
    ]
    for f in (hint.get("files_touched") or [])[:20]:
        lines.append(f"  - {f}")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("design_cites:")
    for c in (hint.get("design_cites") or [])[:10]:
        lines.append(f"  - {c}")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("commands_run (last 15):")
    for cmd in (hint.get("commands_run") or [])[-15:]:
        lines.append(f"  - {cmd}")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _format_memory_fallback(memory_tail: str) -> str:
    """Format Karpathy section 5 Layer-2 fallback into preload block."""
    return (
        "PRE-COMPACT FALLBACK (compact_hint.json stale/absent - MEMORY.md tail):\n"
        f"{memory_tail}\n"
        "(end MEMORY.md fallback)"
    )


def _append_telemetry(record: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Append telemetry per audit-action-loop.md Wire stage. Best-effort; no fail-closed."""
    try:
        STATE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with TELEMETRY_PATH.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(json.dumps(record) + "\n")
    except Exception as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(f"[precompact_hint_emitter] telemetry append failed: {exc!r}\n")


def main() -> int:
    payload = _read_stdin_payload()
    hint = _load_fresh_hint()

    if hint is not None:
        body = _format_hint_payload(hint)
        source = "compact_hint_fresh"
    else:
        body = _format_memory_fallback(_load_memory_fallback())
        source = "memory_md_fallback"

    # Cap to <=9500 chars per Anthropic 10K stdout limit
    if len(body) > STDOUT_CAP_CHARS:
        body = body[:STDOUT_CAP_CHARS - 30] + "\n... [TRUNCATED at 9500 chars]"

    # Emit to stdout - PreCompact routes to "Additional Instructions:" semantic
    sys.stdout.write(body + "\n")

    _append_telemetry({
        "schema": "precompact_hint_emitter.v1",
        "ts": _now_iso(),
        "wire_event": "PreCompact",
        "source": source,
        "trigger": payload.get("trigger", "unknown"),
        "session_id": payload.get("session_id"),
        "agent_id": payload.get("agent_id"),
        "agent_type": payload.get("agent_type"),
        "model": payload.get("model"),
        "transcript_path": payload.get("transcript_path"),
        "body_chars": len(body),
        "hint_present": hint is not None,
    })

    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

Fires on every user prompt; estimates context-window usage; routes hints via
Anthropic CC contract:
  - WARN (>=600k): emit hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext (advisory)
  - HIGH (>=650k): emit additionalContext + systemMessage (visible advisory)
  - CRIT (>=700k): emit additionalContext + systemMessage (visible advisory)

Sidecar write: .claude/state/context_window_sidecar.json (via _atomic_jsonl_append.py

Sister-rule integration:

- karpathy-adapted.md section 5 (Wiki Compounding Surface) — Karpathy "outsource
  thinking vs understanding" framing (the discipline WHY, NOT the number)
- evidence-policy.md Stuck Detection (operator-discipline at threshold escalation)

CAVEAT (per CC team-orch-patterns.md section Context Budget): context-window estimate
from transcript_path token counts; tokens-used may be unavailable in payload.
Conservative threshold trips on estimate floor.

def _int_env(name: str, default: int) -> int:
    raw = os.getenv(name)
    if raw is None or raw == "":
        return default
    try:
        return int(raw)
    except ValueError:
        return default

def _now_iso() -> str:
    return _dt.datetime.now(_dt.timezone.utc).isoformat()


def _read_stdin_payload() -> dict[str, Any]:
    try:
        raw = sys.stdin.read() or ""
        return json.loads(raw) if raw.strip() else {}
    except Exception:
        return {}


def _estimate_tokens_used(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> int | None:
    """Best-effort context-window estimate.

    W174 P0b FIX (follow-up to commit 02f72fd): session-keyed lookup.

    Prior Strategy 3 iterated `data.values()` and returned the first non-zero
    `total_input_tokens` found — which for a multi-session sidecar leaked a
    SIBLING session's reading into this session's gate. Telemetry confirmed
    three distinct sessions (70bd13e6, b2a9dc5b, cd57ff20) all reported at
    658,019 — the alphabetically-first key (1aeadaf1)'s real number.

    Canonical sidecar shape is session-keyed, NOT flat. Both writers and the
    sibling reader agree on this:
      - Writer: .claude/hooks/scripts/context_window_statusline.sh:54-65
        does `data[session_id] = row` (session-keyed insert).
      - Sibling reader: .claude/hooks/scripts/context_window_guard.py:48
        does `data.get(session_id)` (session-keyed lookup).
    The "flat shape" comment in commit 02f72fd reflected an incorrect premise
    about the sidecar layout.

    Revised strategy:
    1. Payload-provided usage if CC ever exposes it (ideal future).
    2. Session-keyed sidecar lookup: data[session_id].total_input_tokens
       (matches sibling context_window_guard.py:48 selection logic).
    3. None -> severity UNKNOWN -> no emit, no block (fail-open per cardinal-rule 7).

    SOTA references:
    - UserPromptSubmit payload includes session_id field:
      https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks:743-757 [VERIFIED 2026-05-13]
    - Sibling lookup pattern (in-repo authoritative):
      .claude/hooks/scripts/context_window_guard.py:40-49 @ HEAD 02f72fd9
    - Sidecar writer (session-keyed shape source-of-truth):
      .claude/hooks/scripts/context_window_statusline.sh:54-65 @ HEAD 02f72fd9
    """
    # Strategy 1: payload-provided usage (ideal-future contract)
    usage = payload.get("usage") or payload.get("context_usage") or {}
    if isinstance(usage, dict):
        tokens = usage.get("input_tokens") or usage.get("total_tokens")
        if isinstance(tokens, (int, float)) and tokens > 0:
            return int(tokens)

    # Strategy 2: session-keyed sidecar lookup. No cross-session leak possible —
    # we only ever read the row for THIS session_id.
    session_id = payload.get("session_id")
    if not isinstance(session_id, str) or not session_id:
        return None
    try:
        if SIDECAR_PATH.exists():
            with SIDECAR_PATH.open(encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                data = json.load(fh)
            if isinstance(data, dict):
                row = data.get(session_id)
                if isinstance(row, dict):
                    tokens = row.get("total_input_tokens")
                    if isinstance(tokens, (int, float)) and tokens > 0:
                        return int(tokens)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        pass

    # Strategy 3: fail-open per cardinal-rule 7 silent-fallback prohibition
    return None


def _emit_warn(tokens: int) -> None:
    """>=WARN threshold: advisory additionalContext only."""
    notice = (
        f"CONTEXT-WINDOW WARN: estimated {tokens:,} tokens used (~{tokens/1000:.0f}k) "
        f"crosses WARN threshold {THRESH_WARN:,}. Approaching Thariq rot zone "
        "(300-400k on Opus 4.7 per claude-thariq-tips-16-apr-26.md:28). "
        "Consider /compact <hint> per auto-compact-discipline.md Rank #3 to pre-empt "
        "blind autocompact."
    )
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
        "hookSpecificOutput": {
            "hookEventName": "UserPromptSubmit",
            "additionalContext": notice,
        }
    }))


def _emit_high(tokens: int) -> None:
    """>=HIGH threshold: advisory + systemMessage visible advisory."""
    notice = (
        f"CONTEXT-WINDOW HIGH: estimated {tokens:,} tokens (~{tokens/1000:.0f}k) "
        f"crosses HIGH threshold {THRESH_HIGH:,}. At/past Thariq rot threshold "
        "(300-400k per claude-thariq-tips-16-apr-26.md:28). STRONGLY recommend "
        "/compact <hint> NOW per auto-compact-discipline.md Rank #3."
    )
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
        "hookSpecificOutput": {
            "hookEventName": "UserPromptSubmit",
            "additionalContext": notice,
        },
        "systemMessage": (
            f"[context-threshold] HIGH ({tokens:,} tokens). Run /compact <hint> "
            "before autocompact fires blind (CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE)."
        ),
    }))


def _emit_crit_advisory(tokens: int) -> None:
    """>=CRIT threshold below 80%: advisory + systemMessage visible advisory."""
    notice = (
        f"CONTEXT-WINDOW CRITICAL: estimated {tokens:,} tokens (~{tokens/1000:.0f}k) "
        f"exceeds CRIT threshold {THRESH_CRIT:,}. Run /compact <hint> with focused "
        "goal/files/cites/commands/test-state/next-action per "
        "auto-compact-discipline.md Rank #3 before blind autocompact "
        "(CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE). "
        "To re-tune for 1M-ctx, set CONTEXT_WINDOW_COMPACT_CRIT_TOKENS in "
        ".claude/settings.json env block."
    )
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
        "hookSpecificOutput": {
            "hookEventName": "UserPromptSubmit",
            "additionalContext": notice,
        },
        "systemMessage": (
            f"[context-threshold] CRIT ({tokens:,} tokens). Run /compact <hint> "
            "before autocompact fires blind (CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE)."
        ),
    }))


# NOTE (W174 P0a/P0b fix-forward): prior _write_sidecar() wrote from this
# hook into context_window_sidecar.json and risked corrupting the canonical
# statusline-owned layout. The canonical sidecar is session-keyed:
# data[session_id] = {"session_id": session_id,
#                     "total_input_tokens": N,
#                     "updated_at": "...", ...}
# This hook treats that shared file as READ-ONLY; the statusline pipeline owns
# writes. Per-fire telemetry continues to land in
# userpromptsubmit_compact_threshold.jsonl (separate file, no shared-shape
# contract).


def _append_telemetry(record: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    try:
        STATE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with TELEMETRY_PATH.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(json.dumps(record) + "\n")
    except Exception as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(f"[userpromptsubmit_compact_threshold] telemetry failed: {exc!r}\n")


def main() -> int:
    payload = _read_stdin_payload()
    tokens = _estimate_tokens_used(payload)

    severity = "UNKNOWN"
    exit_code = 0

    if tokens is None:
        severity = "UNKNOWN"
    elif tokens >= THRESH_CRIT:
        severity = "CRIT"
        _emit_crit_advisory(tokens)
    elif tokens >= THRESH_HIGH:
        severity = "HIGH"
        _emit_high(tokens)
    elif tokens >= THRESH_WARN:
        severity = "WARN"
        _emit_warn(tokens)
    else:
        severity = "OK"

    _append_telemetry({
        "schema": "userpromptsubmit_compact_threshold.v1",
        "ts": _now_iso(),
        "wire_event": "UserPromptSubmit",
        "session_id": payload.get("session_id"),
        "agent_id": payload.get("agent_id"),
        "agent_type": payload.get("agent_type"),
        "model": payload.get("model"),
        "transcript_path": payload.get("transcript_path"),
        "tokens_estimated": tokens,
        "severity": severity,
        "thresh_warn": THRESH_WARN,
        "thresh_high": THRESH_HIGH,
        "thresh_crit": THRESH_CRIT,
        "atomic_available": _ATOMIC_AVAILABLE,
    })

    return exit_code


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

## The rule

When working in long-arc /loop sessions (≥4h wall-clock OR multi-Bundle ship cycles OR cron-driven autonomous arcs), context bloat dominates token cost. The local runtime treats late blind autocompact as a failure mode: CCBP documents the upstream default as roughly 95 unless overridden (`Z:/repos/deps/claude-code-best-practice-shan/best-practice/claude-settings.md:826 @ HEAD 48f2cebeb88b389b27231c418ceadb65baf813fd`), while this repo may set a lower local target in `.claude/settings.json`. Blind autocompact produces lossy summaries (per `karpathy-adapted.md §5`). SOTA auto-compact discipline is **pre-emptive, ranked, and routes-around the autocompact mechanism entirely**.

## Ranked recipe (codex T1 ranking from /goal P2[B] partial trace 2026-05-13)

### Rank #1 — context-mode `ctx_batch_execute` (PRIMARY, ~98% savings)

**When**: any command/probe/script producing >20 lines of output. Multi-command batches with multiple search queries.

**How**:
```
mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_batch_execute(
  commands: [{label, command}, ...],
  queries: [<5-8 specific questions>],
  concurrency: 4-8 for I/O-bound batches
)
```

Raw stdout/output indexed into FTS5 in subprocess sandbox; only the search-result excerpts enter context. **Single batch_execute call replaces 30+ ctx_execute + 10+ ctx_search calls**.

**Sub-variants**:
- `ctx_execute(language: shell|python|javascript, code, intent: "...")` — single command with intent → indexed if output >5KB, returns titled previews
- `ctx_execute_file(path, language, code)` — read+process file content in sandbox; only printed result enters context
- `ctx_fetch_and_index(requests: [{url, source}], concurrency: 4-8)` — replaces WebFetch; raw HTML stays in sandbox, ~3KB preview + searchable knowledge base

### Rank #2 — repomix pack→grep workflow (~70% compression for repo-scope audits)

**When**: line-by-line auditing a `Z:/repos/deps/<repo>` subtree spanning ≥5 files. Replaces 10+ Read calls.

**How** (per `Z:/repos/deps/repomix/src/mcp/mcpServer.ts:20-23 @ HEAD 7dfd2b96`):
1. **Pack**: `mcp__repomix__pack_codebase(directory, compress=true)` → returns `outputId`. Tree-sitter compression ~70% per `Z:/repos/deps/repomix/README.md:1089 @ 7dfd2b96`.
2. **Grep**: `mcp__repomix__grep_repomix_output(outputId, pattern, contextLines=5)` for incremental retrieval — preferred over re-packing uncompressed per README:979.
3. **Skill persist** (if learning is durably reusable): **DO NOT** use `mcp__repomix__generate_skill(directory, skillName)` for routine auto-compact reuse — that primitive writes `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` outside the documented install/provenance path, violating cardinal-rule-5 install-priority + cardinal-rule-6 official-native-channel. Instead: (a) persist topic-scoped findings to `.claude/projects/*/memory/` per Karpathy §5 Layer-3 compiled wiki (no install-class artifact created), OR (b) escalate as install-class candidate via sota-researcher dispatch with convergence-gate Axis-1+2+3 verification + Section 14 marketplace install path + `docs/install-provenance.md` row. Local `generate_skill` invocations bypass T1+T2 audit and provenance log.

### Rank #3 — Pre-emptive `/compact <hint>` (superpowers + Karpathy §5 layered)

**When**: context approaches 300k tokens (rot threshold on Opus 4.7 per Thariq 2026-04-16 at `coordination.md §12 Rewind-first` row Mid-task hint). **NEVER let CC autocompact fire blind at the local target/default boundary**.

**How**: invoke `/compact` with a focused hint that steers the lossy summary toward retained-value content:
```
/compact focus on Bundle ship cumulative state and active queue, drop verbose codex T1 verdict bodies
```

Per `coordination.md §12` row 2: hint steered summary BEFORE rot dominates. Karpathy §5 Layer-3 compiled wiki is the equivalent persistent-storage discipline.

## Supporting disciplines (Rank #4-#7)

### Rank #4 — Rewind-first on failure (coordination.md §12)

When an approach fails mid-iteration, prefer `/rewind` to last sound state over layering corrections. Drops failed-tail + retains good reads. Per Thariq table at `coordination.md §12`:

| Situation | Use | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Explored N files, tried approach A, failed | **Rewind** to after-reads, re-prompt with learning | Keep expensive reads, drop failed attempt |
| Session bloated mid-task | `/compact <hint>` | Steered lossy summary |
| Genuinely new task | `/clear` + brief | Zero rot, controlled carry-over |
| High-volume exploration, only conclusion matters | Subagent fork | Tool noise GC'd on exit |

### Rank #5 — Karpathy §5 3-layer progressive disclosure

Per `karpathy-adapted.md §5 Wiki Compounding Surface`:
- **Layer 1 chronological log**: `.claude/state/*.jsonl` (codex_review_HEAD_*.jsonl / codex_consult_*_OUT.txt / mcp_health.jsonl / subagent_transcripts.jsonl)
- **Layer 2 index**: `.claude/projects/*/memory/MEMORY.md` (≤200 lines / 150-char one-line topic pointers)
- **Layer 3 compiled wiki**: `docs/karpathy-llm-wiki-practice.md` + `.claude/rules/*.md` + per-topic `memory/` files

**MEMORY.md discipline**: NEVER write content directly; always one-line pointer with `[Title](file.md) — hook` format. If a top entry exceeds ~3000 chars, archive immediately (this rule's codification trigger).

### Rank #6 — Pre-emptive arg truncation (deepagents pattern, doc-only port)

Per `Z:/repos/deps/deepagents/.../summarization.py:122-149 @ 95f845d2`: TruncateArgsSettings TypedDict — for long-arc /loop fires touching Edit/Write/execute args with content >4KB, retain only first ~20-1000 chars of the arg with a `"[truncated — N chars; see file/commit for full content]"` placeholder. NOT active middleware in claude-sota-installed (no Python SDK runtime) — but discipline applies operationally: when args bloat, persist the full content to disk first (Write tool), then reference path in subsequent steps.

### Rank #7 — Subagent forks for high-output exploration

Per `parallel-agent-wave.md §Fork-vs-fresh routing` + `team-orch-patterns.md §1M context calibration`: dispatch tool-noisy exploration into subagent fork (forked = inherits parent context, conversation-history-cached) OR fresh subagent (zero parent context, isolation). The subagent's tool output GC'd on exit — only the final return enters parent context.

## How to apply (operational checklist)

For every long-arc /loop fire:

1. **At session start**: check `[████░░░] N/1000k` context indicator. If >20% at start, immediately invoke `/compact <hint>` BEFORE any work
2. **For every >20-line probe**: route through `ctx_batch_execute` (multi-command + queries) OR `ctx_execute` (single command + intent)
3. **For every repo-scope audit ≥5 files**: pack with repomix BEFORE Reading individual files
4. **For every URL fetch**: prefer `ctx_fetch_and_index` over `WebFetch` (raw HTML stays in sandbox)
5. **At ~250k context**: invoke `/compact <hint>` pre-emptively (NOT wait for blind autocompact at the local target/default boundary)
6. **At ~300k context**: STOP planning new work; ship current Bundle + commit + `/clear` between Bundle cycles
7. **On approach-failure**: rewind to last-sound-state with `/rewind`, NEVER layer corrections
8. **MEMORY.md hygiene**: if any entry exceeds ~300 chars or grows beyond a single line of pointer text, immediately archive + reset to proper one-line index format

## Anti-patterns

- **Let autocompact fire blind at the local target/default boundary** — refuted by `karpathy-adapted.md §5` + Thariq tip 2026-04-16. Autocompact at the model's "least intelligent point" produces lossy summaries with no operator steering. Pre-emptive `/compact <hint>` is the SOTA.
- **Read large files into context for analysis** — refuted by file_writing_policy + ctx_execute discipline. Use `ctx_execute_file(path, code)` to process in sandbox; only printed answer enters context.
- **Bash for >20-line commands** — refuted by PreToolUse hook guidance. Route through `ctx_execute(language: shell)` or `ctx_batch_execute`.
- **Multiple ctx_execute calls when one batch suffices** — refuted by ctx_batch_execute description. One call replaces 30+ ctx_execute + 10+ ctx_search calls.
- **Repeated Read of same large file** — refuted by progressive disclosure. Read once, persist findings to a topic-scoped memory file, reference from there.
- **MEMORY.md content-as-entries** (writing content directly into the index) — refuted by Karpathy §5 Layer-2 vs Layer-3 distinction. Index = pointers; content = linked files.
- **Subagent for sub-1000-token operations** — refuted by `parallel-agent-wave.md §Fork-vs-fresh`. Subagent overhead > savings for trivial ops.

## When NOT to apply

- **Short sessions (<10 turns total)**: discipline overhead exceeds savings
- **Interactive debugging single-file edits**: `/compact` interrupts flow; routine Edit+Read suffices
- **Hot-path tool calls where every ms counts**: ctx_execute subprocess startup adds ~50-200ms; not worth on single-line `git status`
- **Files <100 lines or outputs <20 lines**: just use Read/Bash directly

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""PreCompact guard that blocks hintless proactive auto-compaction.

SOTA:
- PreCompact trigger/custom_instructions input and block semantics:
  https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks:1950-1971 [VERIFIED 2026-05-13]
- JSON decision:block contract:
  https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks:725-792 [VERIFIED 2026-05-13]
- Proactive /compact at ~300k before autocompact:
  Z:/claude-sota-installed/.claude/rules/coordination.md:182-190
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path("Z:/claude-sota-installed")
SIDECAR = ROOT / ".claude/state/context_window_sidecar.json"
HARD_LIMIT_PERCENT = float(os.getenv("CONTEXT_WINDOW_HARD_LIMIT_PERCENT", "80"))


def _load_stdin() -> dict:
    try:
        payload = json.loads(sys.stdin.read() or "{}")
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return {}
    return payload if isinstance(payload, dict) else {}


def _load_used(session_id: str) -> float | None:
    try:
        with SIDECAR.open(encoding="utf-8") as f:
            data = json.load(f)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return None
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        return None
    row = data.get(session_id)
    if not isinstance(row, dict):
        return None
    try:
        return float(row.get("used_percentage"))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None


def _block(reason: str) -> None:
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({"decision": "block", "reason": reason}, ensure_ascii=True))


def main() -> int:
    event = _load_stdin()
    if event.get("trigger") != "auto":
        return 0
    if str(event.get("custom_instructions") or "").strip():
        return 0
    session_id = event.get("session_id")
    if not session_id:
        return 0
    used = _load_used(str(session_id))
    if used is None or used >= HARD_LIMIT_PERCENT:
        return 0
    _block(
        f"Blocked hintless proactive auto-compact at {used:.1f}% context. "
        "Run `/compact <hint>` manually with goal, files touched, source citations, "
        "commands run, test state, unresolved risks, and next action. "
        "If this was recovery from an actual context-limit API error, retry after "
        "allowing the recovery compact."
    )
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

    try:
        payload = json.loads(sys.stdin.read() or "{}")
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return {}
    return payload if isinstance(payload, dict) else {}


def _load_used(session_id: str) -> float | None:
    try:
        with SIDECAR.open(encoding="utf-8") as f:
            data = json.load(f)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return None
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        return None
    row = data.get(session_id)
    if not isinstance(row, dict):
        return None
    try:
        return float(row.get("used_percentage"))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None


def _block(reason: str) -> None:
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({"decision": "block", "reason": reason}, ensure_ascii=True))


def main() -> int:
    event = _load_stdin()
    if event.get("trigger") != "auto":
        return 0
    if str(event.get("custom_instructions") or "").strip():
        return 0
    session_id = event.get("session_id")
    if not session_id:
        return 0
    used = _load_used(str(session_id))
    if used is None or used >= HARD_LIMIT_PERCENT:
        return 0
    _block(
        f"Blocked hintless proactive auto-compact at {used:.1f}% context. "
        "Run `/compact <hint>` manually with goal, files touched, source citations, "
        "commands run, test state, unresolved risks, and next action. "
        "If this was recovery from an actual context-limit API error, retry after "
        "allowing the recovery compact."
    )
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# precompact_priorities.sh
#
# Claude Code fires PreCompact before each /compact (manual) and each
# auto compaction. This script's trimmed stdout becomes the
# "Additional Instructions:" block appended after the default 9-section
# compact prompt.
#
# Each rule below is a fidelity requirement layered onto one of the
# existing default sections (1-9) rather than a parallel taxonomy, so
# the summarizer has one coherent shape to fill.
#
# The quoted heredoc delimiter ('PRIORITY_BLOCK') disables every form of
# shell expansion, so apostrophes, em-dashes, and backticks in the block
# pass through untouched with zero escaping.

<priority-preservation-instructions>
These requirements augment the 9 required sections. They do not replace
any section — they raise the fidelity bar for content categories that
the default prompt leaves under-specified.

A. UNANSWERED QUESTIONS (patches §6 and §7)
   The default §6 says to list ALL user messages but does not ask you
   to flag which ones went unanswered. For each §6 message, mark it as
   answered, partially answered, or unanswered. In §7, add a
   sub-heading "Pending Questions" at the top and list every
   unanswered or partially answered user question verbatim.

B. ROOT CAUSES, NOT SYMPTOMS (patches §4 and §5)
   The default §4 asks for "errors and fixes" but does not distinguish
   confirmed root causes from ruled-out hypotheses. In §5, record
   every confirmed root cause with its file path and line number
   (pattern: `path/to/file.py:42`). In §4, keep ruled-out hypotheses
   so they don't get re-tried. Never paraphrase an error message,
   error code, or stack frame — preserve them verbatim.

C. EXACT NUMBERS AND IDS (patches §3, §4, §5)
   The default prompt nowhere tells you to preserve exact digits. Do
   so everywhere they appear: benchmark results, profiling output,
   error rates, latencies, token counts, costs, PR numbers, issue
   numbers, commit SHAs, run IDs, dataset names, and model IDs. Never
   round, never paraphrase a quantitative value.

D. FILE PATH IMPORTANCE TIERS (patches §3)
   The default §3 lists files flat. Group them by importance instead:
   critical (caused or fixed the issue), referenced (read for
   context), mentioned (appeared in discussion only). Use the pattern
   `path/to/file.py:42` whenever a specific line matters.

E. SUBAGENT FINDINGS ARE PRIMARY EVIDENCE (patches §3 and §5)
   The default prompt does not call out Task / Agent tool results.
   For every such tool result in the transcript, preserve the agent's
   final report in full in §3 or §5 as appropriate — file paths, code
   references, citations, and quantitative findings it returned.
   Subagent runs are expensive to redo; treat their reports as
   primary evidence, not as compressible chatter.

F. A-VS-B COMPARISONS (patches §1)
   The default §1 asks for explicit requests and intents but says
   nothing about alternatives under evaluation. When the user was
   weighing option A vs option B (tool X vs tool Y, approach 1 vs
   approach 2), preserve both sides and the decision criteria. If a
   decision was reached, record which side won and the reasoning.

Priority when cutting for length: if A–F would otherwise be dropped
to fit within a section's length, drop conversational filler,
repeated tool output, and intermediate reasoning first.

#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * PreCompact hook for context-mode session continuity.
 *
 * Triggered when Claude Code is about to compact the conversation.
 * Reads all captured session events, builds a priority-sorted resume
 * snapshot (<2KB XML), and stores it for injection after compact.
 *
 * Crash-resilience: wrapped via runHook (#414).
 */

import { runHook } from "./run-hook.mjs";

await runHook(async () => {
  const {
    readStdin,
    parseStdin,
    getSessionId,
    getSessionDBPath,
    resolveConfigDir,
  } = await import("./session-helpers.mjs");
  const { createSessionLoaders } = await import("./session-loaders.mjs");
  const { appendFileSync } = await import("node:fs");
  const { join, dirname } = await import("node:path");
  const { fileURLToPath } = await import("node:url");

  // Resolve absolute path for imports
  const HOOK_DIR = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
  const { loadSessionDB, loadSnapshot } = createSessionLoaders(HOOK_DIR);
  const DEBUG_LOG = join(resolveConfigDir(), "context-mode", "precompact-debug.log");

  try {
    const raw = await readStdin();
    const input = parseStdin(raw);

    const { buildResumeSnapshot } = await loadSnapshot();
    const { SessionDB } = await loadSessionDB();

    const dbPath = getSessionDBPath();
    const db = new SessionDB({ dbPath });
    const sessionId = getSessionId(input);

    // Get all events for this session
    const events = db.getEvents(sessionId);

    if (events.length > 0) {
      const stats = db.getSessionStats(sessionId);
      const snapshot = buildResumeSnapshot(events, {
        compactCount: (stats?.compact_count ?? 0) + 1,
      });

      db.upsertResume(sessionId, snapshot, events.length);
      db.incrementCompactCount(sessionId);

      // Write compaction category event for analytics
      const fileEvents = events.filter(e => e.category === "file");
      db.insertEvent(sessionId, {
        type: "compaction_summary",
        category: "compaction",
        data: `Session compacted. ${events.length} events, ${fileEvents.length} files touched.`,
        priority: 1,
      }, "PreCompact");
    }

    db.close();
  } catch (err) {
    try {
      appendFileSync(DEBUG_LOG, `[${new Date().toISOString()}] ${err.message}\n`);
    } catch {
      // Silent fallback
    }
  }

  // PreCompact doesn't need hookSpecificOutput
  console.log(JSON.stringify({}));
});

Z:\repos\deps\get-shit-done\agents\gsd-code-fixer.md:587:**ALWAYS run inside the isolated worktree** — set up via `branch=$(git branch --show-current)` + `wt=$(mktemp -d "/tmp/sv-${padded_phase}-reviewfix-XXXXXX")` + `git worktree add -b "$reviewfix_branch" "$wt" "$branch"` at the very start (see `setup_worktree` step). Using `mktemp` ensures concurrent runs do not collide. Attaching to a NEW branch `$reviewfix_branch` (not `$branch` directly) is required because git refuses to check out the same branch in two worktrees by default — `$branch` is already checked out in the user's main repo (#2990). Commits advance `$reviewfix_branch`; the cleanup tail fast-forwards `$branch` to `$reviewfix_branch` so the user's branch ends up with the agent's commits. Every file read, edit, and commit must happen inside `$wt`. Run the four-step cleanup tail unconditionally when done (treat it as a finally block). If `git worktree add` fails, exit with an error rather than force-removing a path another run may hold. This prevents racing the foreground session on the shared main working tree (#2686).

Component throws TypeError during render\n\n------------------------\n\n# React Compiler hoists closure property accesses into cache keys, causing TypeError\n\n## Summary\n\nThe React Compiler generates memoization cache keys by eagerly evaluating property accesses that were originally deferred inside closures (event handlers). This causes `TypeError` at render time when the object is `null`/`undefined`, even though the original code would never access the property during render.\n\nEarly returns (`if (!x) return null`) do not help — the compiler hoists the cache key check above the guard.\n\nJSX expressions are not affected — the compiler correctly extracts them to intermediate variables.\n\n## Reproduction\n\n[React Compiler Playground](https://playground.react.dev/)\n\n### Minimal case\n\n```jsx\nconst MyComponent = ({ user }) => {\n  const handleClick = () => {\n    console.log(user.name);\n  };\n\n  if (!user) return null;\n\n  return <button onClick={handleClick}>Click</button>;\n};\n```\n\nCompiled output:\n\n```js\nconst MyComponent = (t0) => {\n  const $ = _c(4);\n  const { user } = t0;\n\n  // Cache key runs BEFORE the null guard — throws when user is null\n  if ($[0] !== user.name) {\n    t1 = () => {\n      console.log(user.name);\n    };\n    $[0] = user.name;\n    $[1] = t1;\n  }\n\n  // The null guard comes AFTER — too late\n  if (!user) {\n    return null;\n  }\n\n  // ...\n};\n```\n\nThe source code is safe: `user.name` is only inside a click handler, and the early return prevents the button from rendering when `user` is null. But the compiler hoists `user.name` into a cache key that runs on **every render**, before the guard.\n\n### With nested access and JSX\n\n```jsx\nconst MyComponent = ({ user }) => {\n  const [visible, setVisible] = useState(false);\n  const [link, setLink] = useState(null);\n\n  const handleClick = async () => {\n    console.log(user.company.id);\n    console.log(user.email);\n  };\n\n  return (\n    <div onClick={() => setVisible(false)}>\n      <span>{user?.email}</span>\n      <button onClick={handleClick}>Click</button>\n    </div>\n  );\n};\n```\n\nCompiled output (simplified):\n\n```js\n// The compiler hoists user.company.id and user.email from the closure\n// into cache key checks that run on EVERY render:\nif ($[0] !== user.company.id || $[1] !== user.email) {\n    t1 = async () => {\n      console.log(user.company.id);\n      console.log(user.email);\n    };\n    $[0] = user.company.id;\n    $[1] = user.email;\n    $[2] = t1;\n}\n\n// JSX — correctly extracted to variable (safe)\nconst t4 = user?.email;\nif ($[7] !== t4) {\n    t5 = <span>{t4}</span>;\n}\n```\n\n## Expected behavior\n\nThe compiler should not introduce runtime errors that the source code would not produce. Property accesses hoisted from closures into cache keys should be guarded, e.g. by extracting to intermediate variables:\n\n```js\nconst t0 = user?.name;\nif ($[0] !== t0) {\n    t1 = () => {\n      console.log(user.name);\n    };\n    $[0] = t0;\n    $[1] = t1;\n}\n```\n\n## Workarounds\n\n### 1. Extract to variables\n\nExtract property accesses into variables before using them in closures. The compiler then caches on the primitive values:\n\n```jsx\nconst companyId = user?.company?.id;\nconst email = user?.email;\n\nconst handleClick = async () => {\n  console.log(companyId);\n  console.log(email);\n};\n```\n\n### 2. Add optional chaining to every closure access\n\nAdding `?.` to every property access inside closures makes the compiler preserve it in cache keys. Note that **every** access must have `?.` — missing it on even one will produce an unsafe cache key for that property path:\n\n```jsx\nconst handleClick = async () => {\n  console.log(user?.company.id);\n  console.log(user?.email);\n};\n```\n\n### 3. Use nullish coalescing on destructuring\n\nUsing `?? {}` when destructuring the nullable object anywhere in the component signals to the compiler that the value can be nullish. This makes the compiler generate `?.` in **all** cache keys for that object:\n\n```jsx\nconst handleClick = () => {\n  const { name, email } = user ?? {};\n  console.log(name, email);\n};\n```\n\nThis produces `$[x] !== user?.name` instead of `$[x] !== user.name` in cache keys across the component.\n\n### 4. Add a null guard inside the closure\n\nAdding a null check before the property access inside the closure makes the compiler use the **object reference** as the cache key instead of the property path:\n\n```jsx\nconst handleClick = () => {\n  if (!user) return;\n  console.log(user.company.id);\n  console.log(user.email);\n};\n```\n\nThis produces `$[x] !== user` (the reference) instead of `$[x] !== user.company.id` (the property access) in the cache key. Comparing a reference to `null`/`undefined` never throws.\n\n## Environment\n\n- React Compiler (babel plugin via `react-compiler-runtime`)\n- Webpack 5 with HMR\n- Observed in both HMR hot-update bundles and regular builds\n\n\n### How often does this bug happen?\n\nEvery time\n\n### What version of React are you using?\n\n18.3.1\n\n### What version of React Compiler are you using?\n\n1.0.0","createdAt":"2026-02-11T13:34:24Z","labels":[{"id":"MDU6TGFiZWw0MDkyOTE1MQ==","name":"Type: Bug","description":"","color":"b60205"},{"id":"MDU6TGFiZWwxNTU5ODQxNjA=","name":"Status: Unconfirmed","description":"A potential issue that we haven't yet confirmed as a bug","color":"d4c5f9"}],"number":35762,"title":"[Compiler Bug]: Closure dependency cache keys eagerly evaluate property accesses, causing TypeError on nullable objects"},{"author":{"id":"U_kgDOBtEQIA","is_bot":false,"login":"rstar327","name":""},"body":"<!--\n  Please provide a clear and concise description of what the bug is. Z:\repos\deps\context-mode\README.md:876:The `ctx_index` tool chunks markdown content by headings while keeping code blocks intact, then stores them in a **SQLite FTS5** (Full-Text Search 5) virtual table. The SQLite backend is selected automatically at runtime: `bun:sqlite` on Bun, `node:sqlite` on Linux + Node.js >= 22.13, and `better-sqlite3` everywhere else. Search uses **BM25 ranking** — a probabilistic relevance algorithm that scores documents based on term frequency, inverse document frequency, and document length normalization. **Porter stemming** is applied at index time so "running", "runs", and "ran" match the same stem. Titles and headings are weighted **5x** in BM25 scoring for precise navigational queries.
